turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm an estate agent and I've got a tiny studio flat to list. How do I make it not look like a shoebox?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Shoot from a corner, standing in a doorway if you can, with the camera at about chest height. That shows the most floor and makes the room feel deeper.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I use the ultra wide on my phone?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Yes, but don't go too wide, or the walls bend and buyers feel tricked. Keep vertical lines straight by holding the phone level.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The owner's stuff is everywhere though.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Clear the surfaces, hide the cables and the bin, make the bed tight. Less clutter honestly reads as more space.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Open the curtains and turn every lamp on. Shoot in the late morning, when the light coming in is bright but not harsh.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good luck with the listing. A bright first photo of the main room will do most of the work.
